spots.name: Boston Common
spots.description: Begin with Boston's long-standing public park, where open lawns and walking paths contrast with busy downtown streets. The public space provides an easy first stop, while seasonal facilities such as Frog Pond can have separate charges.

spots.name: Boston Public Library — Central Library
spots.description: The Central Library at Copley Square offers a thoughtful indoor stop with architectural spaces and exhibitions in a working public institution. It is ideal for a quieter cultural break, but individual tours and rooms may have schedules or access restrictions.

spots.name: Boston Public Garden
spots.description: This landscaped garden is known for plantings, winding paths and a lagoon, creating a more decorative walk than the neighboring Common. Exploring the grounds costs nothing, although the independently operated Swan Boats are an optional ticketed experience.

spots.name: Kerry Park
spots.description: This small Queen Anne viewpoint is known for a classic view of Seattle's skyline and the Space Needle. Plan it as a scenic stop rather than a full-day park, and be mindful of slopes and weather when walking to the overlook.

spots.name: Seattle Central Library
spots.description: The public library's downtown building combines reading spaces and contemporary architecture, making it a rewarding stop even for someone who is not borrowing books. Public access is free, but tours, meeting areas and holiday hours should be checked with the library.

spots.name: Pike Place Market
spots.description: Explore the historic public market district for vendors, stalls and a lively waterfront-adjacent atmosphere. Browsing the public market does not require an admission ticket, but meals, purchases, parking and some experiences are paid.

spots.name: Lincoln Memorial
spots.description: The Lincoln Memorial offers a striking setting for reflecting on U.S. history and the landscape of the National Mall. There is no entrance fee, but access to some facilities can vary, especially during evening hours or public events.

spots.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
spots.description: Explore displays that introduce natural history through collections, scientific research and exhibitions. General admission is free without a pass, making this a practical indoor option, though all visitors must comply with museum screening and access rules.

spots.name: National Gallery of Art
spots.description: The National Gallery connects visitors with art across centuries in its buildings and sculpture spaces. General admission and regular exhibitions are free, while some events may require advance registration despite having no ticket price.

spots.name: Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Gardens
spots.description: The Bellagio conservatory presents large seasonal arrangements of plants and themed displays near the hotel lobby. Public viewing is complimentary, but the space may close for installation changes between seasons, making the current calendar essential.

spots.name: Fremont Street Experience
spots.description: The downtown pedestrian entertainment district offers canopy light displays and public live performances. Walking through the area and many regular shows are free, while zipline rides, casino activities, food and special-ticket events cost extra.

spots.name: Springs Preserve
spots.description: Springs Preserve combines desert-focused exhibitions and outdoor areas in a destination away from the busiest resort corridors. General admission is ticketed, and outdoor activities can be curtailed in extreme heat, so check rates and visitor alerts before choosing a date.

spots.name: Centennial Park
spots.description: Centennial Park provides outdoor paths, green space and views of Nashville's full-scale Parthenon replica. Walking through the public park is free, but going inside the Parthenon museum is a separate ticketed activity.

spots.name: Tennessee State Museum
spots.description: The Tennessee State Museum offers exhibitions about the state's history and culture in a purpose-built public facility. General admission is free, and its location beside Bicentennial Capitol Mall makes it a sensible indoor anchor for a history-focused outing.

spots.name: Bicentennial Capitol Mall State Park
spots.description: Bicentennial Capitol Mall is a public state park that uses monuments, a large map and landscaped paths to tell stories about Tennessee. It offers a natural continuation of a museum visit, though weather, organized events and nearby parking can affect your experience.

spots.name: Pack Square Park
spots.description: This downtown green space brings walking paths, public art and a popular seasonal splashpad into one central area. It's a relaxed family stop, although live programming and splashpad operation need a check before visiting.

spots.name: Asheville Botanical Garden
spots.description: Explore the region's native plants on paths designed for quiet nature study rather than sports. Families are welcome with supervision, but the operator forbids pets except service dogs.

spots.name: Asheville Museum of Science (AMOS)
spots.description: This downtown museum gives children and adults hands-on ways to explore science and the environment. General admission is paid for most visitors, with some age-based and eligibility discounts listed by the museum.

spots.name: White River State Park
spots.description: The canal and surrounding downtown green spaces offer an easy walking outing without buying a museum ticket. Families can explore the paths, while neighboring attractions and boat rentals are separate paid choices.

spots.name: The Children's Museum of Indianapolis
spots.description: Hands-on exhibits connect science, history and creativity for families and younger visitors. Prices vary depending on your visit date, so select tickets on the official site before planning a full museum day.

spots.name: Indianapolis Central Library
spots.description: The Central Library brings a historic limestone structure together with a modern glass-and-steel addition. It offers a quiet indoor setting for books and architecture without a general admission ticket.

spots.name: International Rose Test Garden
spots.description: A large rose garden in Washington Park gives visitors free outdoor paths, planting displays and views of the city. Parking can cost extra and the City of Portland explicitly requires dogs to stay on leash.

spots.name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI)
spots.description: OMSI's interactive science spaces are designed for hands-on discovery across several age groups. General entry is paid, and selected exhibitions, presentations or experiences can require additional tickets.

spots.name: Powell's City of Books
spots.description: The famous independent bookstore provides a city-block collection of books to browse at your own pace. Entry does not require a ticket, but shopping and optional purchases are separate costs.
